findings.message: recoverIntegrationCorrectionStart validates the journal and integration-record hashes but never re-runs assertStartTokenCurrent or assertUniqueCorrectionCheckout before applying the recorded writes. A clean correction ref advanced beyond the token's start commit is therefore accepted during recovery and the stale run/story publication proceeds instead of refusing unchanged. The fresh regression at tests/integration-correction.test.mjs:1072 reaches Missing expected exception.

validateIntegrationCorrectionJournal accepts any second write whose path starts with docs/stories/ and validates the parsed story bytes, but it never requires descriptor.writes[1].path to equal token.story_path. An attacker or corrupted journal can rewrite the descriptor, reconstruction and hashes consistently and redirect publication to a shadow story while the generated run remains bound to the original story. The fresh regression at tests/integration-correction.test.mjs:1097 reaches Missing expected exception.

currentFailureBasis treats any repeatable nonzero merge-tree result with the same Git version as a composition-conflict-no-m basis. It does not distinguish content conflicts from fatal errors, so exit 128 for unrelated histories mints a correction token even though no composition conflict was proved. The fresh regression at tests/integration-correction.test.mjs:1126 reaches Missing expected exception.

assertUniqueCorrectionCheckout captures the correction worktree Git anchor but validates only anchor.head. Initial start does not compare protected ignored entries or protected Git metadata with the recorded I/M checkout proof, and journal recovery does not compare the live protected checkout with the generated run's frozen baseline and full Git anchor. The independent real-Git probe at t05c-protected-probe.test.mjs (SHA-256 3fc1f2a707a3827fdc02901c9aa6329f7d049bfe3c309a97175cf8a2aae607c0) reproduced Missing expected exception for first-start .codex drift, journal .codex drift, started surviving-journal .codex drift, and journal config.worktree drift; all four paths accepted and mutated state. This violates the exact protected I/M checkout and unchanged recovery requirements.

The declared npm test gate at snapshot 405f77cdd37a269fc02bcbdb34c5953b48cac485cd700185db9e6e5ae70cb334 ended FAIL after the runtime's 600-second limit with spawnSync /bin/sh ETIMEDOUT and no complete TAP result. Fresh complete test-gate evidence required by T05C-AC3 is therefore absent. This is separate from the protected-checkout defect; npm run validate passed at the same snapshot.

assertCorrectionProtectedProof is neither a relocation-safe protected-state comparison nor a complete recursive checkout proof. It rejects a clean standard initialized submodule at the exact recorded gitlink and an identical repository-relative .githooks configuration because raw protected hashes contain worktree-specific paths, while a shared-common-dir control accepts moved nested HEAD, changed nested tracked bytes, and a nested skip-worktree flag because recursion compares only protected hashes, protected ignored entries, and initialized-set membership. The independent real-Git probe t05c-nested-mode-probe.test.mjs (SHA-256 02b37f9b1c6977f18596ba16b5fc8b424e2972d747ff2667db9f76d6f35818c7) reproduced both false refusals and all three false acceptances. Correction start therefore cannot enforce the frozen exact-I/M submodule contract without rejecting legitimate worktree relocation.

Recovery replaces the complete live story fingerprint with the retained baseline fingerprint whenever the story text equals the legal after-image, so it also erases evidence that the file mode changed. Real-Git probes at both story and started-record boundaries changed the published story from mode 0600 to 0755 with core.filemode=true; recoverIntegrationCorrectionStart returned recovered:true and preserved mode 0755. The typed journal therefore accepts a state outside its frozen operational snapshot instead of refusing unchanged.

assertRecordSource now applies correction-only source cleanliness and full-anchor checks to every integration-record mutation. This rejects a valid finished source run whose preexisting dirty task input remains unchanged and should instead require fresh M evidence. The fresh full npm test gate completed with 276 tests, 275 PASS and this one FAIL at tests/integration.test.mjs:351; integrate-adopt refuses src/preexisting.txt before mutation. The accepted base supported this workflow, so strict correction-source validation must not replace the ordinary immutable source snapshot rules.

recoverIntegrationCorrectionStart does not enforce the started envelope's retained run/story hashes or require both published after-images before deleting a surviving journal. At integration.mjs:1635-1639 it checks only starting_record_hash and descriptor_identity, then calls applyIntegrationCorrectionJournal; that generic starting-phase applier accepts an absent run or the exact story before-image and writes the after-images. The independent real-Git probe core-worktree-started-probe.test.mjs (SHA-256 fae33daa9a81cd86de3a63f88741d48f91c1d713a22bf69402b8032a7fbb5104) confirmed that recovery returned recovered:true, recreated a deleted run, republished a reverted story, and accepted rehashed unrelated started.run_hash and started.story_hash before deleting the journal. This violates the frozen requirement that a surviving started journal may be deleted only when its retained bindings and both after-images match.

summary: Whole-task review at snapshot 6878683c7c9e3511d86a2d59507c28805816398b43ed8737740dea8a875ea0e3 passes. Fix4 resolves the ninth retained finding; all nine findings are resolved, npm test passes 294/294, npm run validate passes, and no new finding remains.
